name: You Could Have It So Much Better

podcast.body: Their second album, released in October 2005, achieved significant commercial success by reaching number one on the UK charts and placing in the top ten in America. "That was Franz Ferdinand's second album, you could have it so much better."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album, their second, successfully built upon the platinum success of their debut record. "Franz Furtanand's second album, you could have had it so much better, built on the platinum success of their debut record"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 00's Part 3: The Return of Rock

podcast.body: This second album was released on October 5, 2005, approximately 18 months after their debut. The band felt they had "unfinished business" and more ideas to explore from their first record, leading to its quick release. Its visual imagery drew heavily from the Soviet Communist era, characterized by bold, geometric, and blocky designs, even influencing the font choice, to match the music's clean lines, preciseness, and boldness, as well as the "cut and paste" song structures. "And that's why the second record came out so quickly after it was like, come on, this is unfinished business here, we need to do something well with this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
